answer: In the Glacier protocol, each AI agent key must solve a verifiable delay function requiring 10¹⁴ sequential SHA-256 evaluations (the Walnut puzzle) plus burn a nonrefundable 12-USDC mint fee paid by the deployer. Verifiers check the succinct STARK proof on-chain. Because each key requires distinct puzzle entropy, costs scale linearly: N fake Raven identities incur an irreversible loss of 12 × N USDC and 10¹⁴ × N hashes, preventing cheap identity resets.
